chapter: Chicago in the 1950s: Mercury, unions and jobbing
title: Plain Old Blues, small labels and the business of music
summary: Hodes says Plain Old Blues sold well, but Mercury wanted 100,000. He concludes small labels are better.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I found this is the business music, as opposed to the business of playing music. This is the business music. And most musicians don't care for the business of music, and you can see why. There's a thing I never heard of. I'm now a talent scout. If they had paid me for bringing them that tune, it would have been a different thing. Say, here, you brought us
a tune and we want him to do it first because he's got a bigger name, and he's money. They didn't say that, they just held me up.

But nine months later, I was grateful that I had a date, because nobody around town was getting dates. Chicago is not a place to record, if you had a band. It's not a place now to record, as anyone knows, you have to find an angel somewhere. Big companies won't do it. I went up to Mercury after I made "Plain Old Blues", and DownBeat -- it was just fortunate at that month they reviewed the record, it was the only record that got five stars. Because of that, the policy was to buy 250 records, I believe, and give them away with subscriptions.

And that record sold better, I was told, than any of that series that they put out. And I heard -- and I'm not sure it's the truth, but I heard that it had sold as many as 27,000. And I thought, man, that's -- I ought to get a date. And I went up there, and whoever I talked to said, that ain't enough for us.
He'd left. He says, you've got to have at least 100,000 for us to be interested. That'll start making us money.
Sounds like Green, who became President.
And so I didn't get a date. Now, for a

little company, I found out, if I would be ever fortunate enough to sell 2,700 records, they would be in seventh heaven. So the thing I discovered was to record for small labels, as other musicians have discovered, because they will keep you alive, they don't expect that much, they're not in that big business, and you have a voice. Suddenly, you have something to say, it's said.
